Dear Kalinga,

Good day, dear Kalinga! I pray that you and your loved ones are doing well. Because of your help, I am still able to study, and I will always be thankful for that. I am truly thankful that you chose to believe in me and to help me stay in school. I hope you will not mind if I share the important things that happened to me this month.

For this month, I am happy to share that I did well in our first quarter examinations. I am currently in Grade 9, and I received 94 in Values Education and 89 in Araling Panlipunan. My general average for this quarter is 91, which is higher than my average of 88 last quarter. I was chosen to represent our class in the division quiz bee, so my teacher gave me extra reviewers. I have not yet received my grade in MAPEH because the results have not been released.

To continue improving myself, I make short reviewers and read them before going to bed. I joined the school choir, which has helped me become more confident when speaking in front of others.

My father is a security guard in Valenzuela, and my mother is a vendor at the public market. My younger sister is in Grade 7, and I help her with her homework in the evenings. We are thankful that we are all healthy and that we still eat dinner together almost every night.

The printing shop near our school was closed for several days, and the printing of our project was delayed. Fortunately, our teacher moved the deadline, and we submitted it early.

Thank you once again for your kindness, Kalinga. I hope that you will continue to help students like me. May the Lord bless you abundantly for your generosity.

Your scholar,
Lorenzo P. Rivera

Dear Kalinga,

Greetings and good day! I hope that you and everyone in your organization are doing well. I am happy to write to you again and to thank you for your kindness. Allow me to share with you the highlights of my month.

This month was difficult for me. I am currently in my fourth year taking Bachelor of Science in Information Technology, and the results of our midterm examinations were lower than I expected. I received 2.5 in Computer Programming and 2.5 in Data Structures, which are lower than my grades last term. Although I passed, I felt discouraged because I studied for these examinations. I also failed one quiz because I did not understand the lesson, and I was unable to recover from it. I received 2.75 in Discrete Mathematics.

For my studies, I read one news article every day to improve my vocabulary and my understanding of current events.

My father is a tricycle driver in Quezon City, and my mother is a cook in a carinderia. My older brother is working part-time, and my younger sister is in Grade 8. We are all in good health, but we are worried about our expenses.

The income of our family became lower this month because the working days of my father were reduced. My parents are trying to find other ways to earn, but it is not enough for all of our needs. I felt discouraged, and I sometimes thought of stopping school to help them. I know that finishing my studies is the best way to help my family, so I continue to attend my classes.

Thank you for always supporting us, Kalinga. Your scholarship has helped me not only in school but also in my daily needs. I hope to repay your kindness by finishing my studies. May the Lord bless you abundantly for your generosity.

Your scholar,
Bea R. Soriano
